decisions.context: Cameras must detect defects when network access is unavailable. The brief specifies on-device execution but no prediction latency target.

alternatives.label: On-device edge inference
cons: Small-team operations: device rollout to manage

decisions.rationale: Offline inference decides the choice: on-device execution works without a network, at the cost of managing device deployments. This is supported by “Composing Deep-Learning Microservices for the Hybrid Internet of Things” and “Three Levels of ML Software.”
consequences: Each device needs a deployable model runtime.
Devices must receive model updates when connected.

decisions.context: The model is retrained weekly from newly labelled images. The system needs to start training on that cadence.

alternatives.label: Manual retraining trigger
cons: Weekly retraining: depends on a person each week

decisions.rationale: Weekly retraining decides the choice: a schedule starts training consistently without relying on a person to remember each run. “Architecting a Machine Learning Pipeline” and “MLOps: Continuous delivery and automation pipelines in machine learning” document recurring retraining schedules.
consequences: The weekly job must have access to newly labelled images.
Failed runs need a way to be noticed and retried.

decisions.context: Weekly training should use new labels with limited infrastructure and a small team. The brief gives no indication that training needs to exceed one machine.

alternatives.label: Automated retraining pipeline
pros: Weekly retraining: automates recurring model updates

decisions.rationale: Weekly retraining decides the choice: automation makes the recurring update repeatable, while adding pipeline maintenance. “MLOps Principles” and “MLOps: Continuous delivery and automation pipelines in machine learning” describe automated retraining workflows.
consequences: Training and release failures need visible status.
The system needs an operator path for investigating failed runs.

decisions.context: The model is retrained every week, and infrastructure budget is tight. No training duration or data-volume limit is specified.

alternatives.label: Vertically scalable training
pros: Low infrastructure cost: avoids distributed setup
cons: Weekly retraining: limited by one machine’s capacity

alternatives.label: Parallel candidate training
cons: Low infrastructure cost: uses more compute

decisions.rationale: Low infrastructure cost decides the choice: scale on a single larger machine until training duration or capacity requires more, giving up parallel candidate speed. “System Architectures for Personalization and Recommendation” describes vertical scaling, while “MLOps: Methods and Tools of DevOps for Machine Learning” describes parallel candidate training.
consequences: A single machine limits training capacity.
The brief lacks data-volume and training-time targets to set a scaling threshold.

decisions.context: Newly trained models must reach cameras that may be offline. A bad update could disrupt defect detection until a device reconnects.

alternatives.label: Progressive release automation with rollback
pros: Reliable inference: enables incremental rollout and rollback
cons: Small-team operations: rollout process needs setup

alternatives.label: Unified release automation
pros: Weekly rollout: automates build and release
cons: Reliable inference: rollback is not explicit

decisions.rationale: Reliable inference decides the choice: progressive rollout with rollback limits the impact of a faulty update, at the cost of release setup. “Productionizing Machine Learning with a Microservices Architecture” and “MLOps: Model management, deployment, and monitoring with Azure Machine Learning” support progressive releases and rollback.
consequences: Devices need a way to receive updates incrementally.
The previous model version must remain available for rollback.

decisions.context: Weekly retraining produces successive model versions from changing labelled-image datasets. The team needs enough history to identify and restore a known version.

alternatives.label: End-to-end reproducible lifecycle governance
pros: Reproducibility: links data, runs, artifacts, and health

alternatives.label: Artifact version control
cons: Reproducibility: limited training and dataset lineage

decisions.rationale: Reproducibility decides the choice: linking datasets, training runs, and deployed models makes weekly updates traceable, at the cost of added record keeping. “MLOps: What It Is, Why it Matters, and How To Implement It” and “MLOps: Model management, deployment, and monitoring with Azure Machine Learning” describe lifecycle traceability.
consequences: Each release needs associated dataset and training metadata.
The team takes on more tracking work than artifact versioning alone.

decisions.context: The system receives newly labelled images and retrains weekly, but cameras may be offline. Monitoring should reveal input changes and inform model maintenance without relying on a continuous connection.

alternatives.label: Passive production operation
cons: Reliable inference: failures may go unnoticed

decisions.rationale: Reliable inference decides the choice: drift monitoring can flag changed inputs for investigation, with setup and review effort as the trade-off. “MLOps: Continuous delivery and automation pipelines in machine learning” and “MLOps Principles” support monitoring input and feature changes. The design point combines drift monitoring with the weekly schedule and automated retraining; the workspace records no sources adopting that full combination.
consequences: Monitoring results need to be collected when devices reconnect.
Drift alerts require review and do not by themselves establish prediction quality.

uncovered: Main requirements, ranked: inference without network access; weekly retraining and device rollout; tight infrastructure budget; small-team operating effort. The brief provides no latency target, dataset volume or retention policy, model framework, device update protocol, or failure and rollback service-level targets.

The design point check returned no adopting sources for the selected combination. A rival point swapping in model-as-a-service deployment, unified release automation, artifact-only versioning, parallel candidate training, and manual retraining also had no adopting sources. The selected point warned that it combines three values within Production Monitoring and Adaptation; that dimension has zero exclusivity in the workspace, so the monitoring practices are treated as combinable.
